kwargs.question: Explain the theory of relativity in simple terms.

output:
Albert Einstein's theory of relativity, a foundational concept in modern physics, revolutionized our understanding of the universe by altering how we perceive space, time, gravity, and the cosmos itself. It is divided into two main parts: special relativity, introduced in 1905, and general relativity, published in 1915. [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG0tQE9KkECnGYoSOhcMJjESFs-gjo0FXdUiFffXstmip7z0hJ4tFNfq_HMKiRywwBoFMsVb32Vf5WYAcTFRQRpvCgoQfa81uV6GWnv2APiVYhhfSqc0vammP8cgROVvMds-u2uHGWfO3Xrcv_4xQ7U9bcjXQ==) [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG-qrlt57UKl735Vi_bNuaozaKGgb9pRK06eIrPRF10hRfSt4cGZL8OA3IsDqXu5fVngFa3pDYGc8FZGzgmgsrGk3uASQbtbJ5uPbTuJnZdafTSvJoRydCa_8TqdFZS-i1VGIgJg-U5TZjOFeM=)

**Special Relativity**

Special relativity focuses on motion without the influence of gravity. It is built upon two key principles:

*   **The laws of physics are the same for all observers in inertial frames of reference.** This means that the rules of physics remain consistent whether you are standing still or moving at a constant speed in a straight line. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQH7hr6RuGSJZvfVal5Amp82MIfIIHpKWgxvV7TFnQVu6SD2hOzvan50-QLabfartUyQjrXxJdzHMCt4LrftQfa-lcVRqNcEy3viq5Kh3oXO2ZZ1Wdj4nx_E55KchGhcOY2f_z2DPQ==) [dummies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGMFIp3Dx5gN2PAU26kCL6n7SED3kiAG2xPJwATa3OBjZQgT1-8RyYX5EhXNPHrVsJRvuaaQn3sgkq5hmgAh9r2Uu-pbJNAvxOphtb5ssi69zcSoeHW3GM2Hg22TgxxkBMoRzbH_S7qVfWvPNnPnQGNZYWuTKPw9hpn--TXqpl496VHQHcPnZPN4qNRjpREhdhcX5_TX23iU87v2rAI0tiP2Q==)
*   **The speed of light in a vacuum is constant for all observers, regardless of their motion or the motion of the light source.** This unchanging cosmic speed limit is approximately 299,792,458 meters per second. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEGYT-8Xhu3UsjXWaleQl6EF1AKNTAkS1ga2l5hXzm9oRi0ZtS6OsElqIAa6ME949CMDwI5NWfVUKxyewN1s0igZ9ZYiQTDG3KDXTurnsgG_-yhJUKCf93VrKzpMQJYBUJxqDuNWw==)

These postulates lead to some counterintuitive but experimentally confirmed effects:

*   **Time Dilation:** Time is not absolute; it is relative to the observer's motion. Clocks that are moving tick slower than stationary clocks from the perspective of a stationary observer. This effect becomes more noticeable as an object approaches the speed of light. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEGYT-8Xhu3UsjXWaleQl6EF1AKNTAkS1ga2l5hXzm9oRi0ZtS6OsElqIAa6ME949CMDwI5NWfVUKxyewN1s0igZ9ZYiQTDG3KDXTurnsgG_-yhJUKCf93VrKzpMQJYBUJxqDuNWw==) [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG0tQE9KkECnGYoSOhcMJjESFs-gjo0FXdUiFffXstmip7z0hJ4tFNfq_HMKiRywwBoFMsVb32Vf5WYAcTFRQRpvCgoQfa81uV6GWnv2APiVYhhfSqc0vammP8cgROVvMds-u2uHGWfO3Xrcv_4xQ7U9bcjXQ==) For instance, astronaut Scott Kelly experienced time slightly slower than his twin brother Mark during his year-long stay on the International Space Station due to the station's high speed. [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG0tQE9KkECnGYoSOhcMJjESFs-gjo0FXdUiFffXstmip7z0hJ4tFNfq_HMKiRywwBoFMsVb32Vf5WYAcTFRQRpvCgoQfa81uV6GWnv2APiVYhhfSqc0vammP8cgROVvMds-u2uHGWfO3Xrcv_4xQ7U9bcjXQ==)
*   **Length Contraction:** Objects moving at very high speeds appear shorter in the direction of their movement to an observer who is not moving with them. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEGYT-8Xhu3UsjXWaleQl6EF1AKNTAkS1ga2l5hXzm9oRi0ZtS6OsElqIAa6ME949CMDwI5NWfVUKxyewN1s0igZ9ZYiQTDG3KDXTurnsgG_-yhJUKCf93VrKzpMQJYBUJxqDuNWw==)
*   **Relativity of Simultaneity:** Events that appear to happen at the same time for one observer may not be simultaneous for another observer who is moving differently. There is no universal "now" that applies to everyone. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEGYT-8Xhu3UsjXWaleQl6EF1AKNTAkS1ga2l5hXzm9oRi0ZtS6OsElqIAa6ME949CMDwI5NWfVUKxyewN1s0igZ9ZYiQTDG3KDXTurnsgG_-yhJUKCf93VrKzpMQJYBUJxqDuNWw==) [nationalgeographic](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFg44NFFaKayeCeG73vYAmabcIkSsTEY0hjpZZU6E9kJnOVVXqgyv7eyS9EuHyw13GFmdjJDAb1TJ-aQdL0zBATmi8Xdz5Oa9iiKUTk2XCqcfP3RuoMbcX94sD2cjfOHslRr02qL6MPgl5BkocqM_38s5Ii6BUNWNtrmBrAFMBbO-p_ZRavYav1_wbn2Yz30lDWXExh9ZtcdsnJF2esm-hyecQbTLiwWi6Obg==)
*   **Mass-Energy Equivalence:** Famously expressed as E=mc², this principle states that mass and energy are interchangeable. A tiny amount of mass can be converted into a tremendous amount of energy, and vice versa, which is the principle behind nuclear energy and how stars generate light and heat. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEGYT-8Xhu3UsjXWaleQl6EF1AKNTAkS1ga2l5hXzm9oRi0ZtS6OsElqIAa6ME949CMDwI5NWfVUKxyewN1s0igZ9ZYiQTDG3KDXTurnsgG_-yhJUKCf93VrKzpMQJYBUJxqDuNWw==) [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG0tQE9KkECnGYoSOhcMJjESFs-gjo0FXdUiFffXstmip7z0hJ4tFNfq_HMKiRywwBoFMsVb32Vf5WYAcTFRQRpvCgoQfa81uV6GWnv2APiVYhhfSqc0vammP8cgROVvMds-u2uHGWfO3Xrcv_4xQ7U9bcjXQ==)

Special relativity also unified space and time into a single four-dimensional continuum known as **spacetime**. [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGqWowAM_JVqdnChFWM1se3_p4mTWGzHNQpW9yB24RQv_VQNtKUpk29HR740yMA980dABbftXbUFkh-os2jd-BFc712EJ2d2D4wLYr595N8q0YET2TC1BVQjJsOXRZaWRgEpJfwIrINQODovoops1bTYhAoxQ==) [dummies](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGMFIp3Dx5gN2PAU26kCL6n7SED3kiAG2xPJwATa3OBjZQgT1-8RyYX5EhXNPHrVsJRvuaaQn3sgkq5hmgAh9r2Uu-pbJNAvxOphtb5ssi69zcSoeHW3GM2Hg22TgxxkBMoRzbH_S7qVfWvPNnPnQGNZYWuTKPw9hpn--TXqpl496VHQHcPnZPN4qNRjpREhdhcX5_TX23iU87v2rAI0tiP2Q==)

**General Relativity**

General relativity extends special relativity by incorporating gravity. Einstein proposed that gravity is not a force, but rather a consequence of the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGqWowAM_JVqdnChFWM1se3_p4mTWGzHNQpW9yB24RQv_VQNtKUpk29HR740yMA980dABbftXbUFkh-os2jd-BFc712EJ2d2D4wLYr595N8q0YET2TC1BVQjJsOXRZaWRgEpJfwIrINQODovoops1bTYhAoxQ==) [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEWDZKYrR3gNukj5QQ90447emikv_0L2sqwMzy7_9JLxi58q9FPc0heoVqIF9wLQ4_Hh0GlD8H2GhbimKkGMTypjuS3viZscpjRSwH9l6O4VXs_z5zpcf0oaA30oz-HVCnnQzvK6g==)

*   **Spacetime Curvature:** Massive objects warp the fabric of spacetime around them, similar to how a heavy ball placed on a stretched rubber sheet creates a dip. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQH7hr6RuGSJZvfVal5Amp82MIfIIHpKWgxvV7TFnQVu6SD2hOzvan50-QLabfartUyQjrXxJdzHMCt4LrftQfa-lcVRqNcEy3viq5Kh3oXO2ZZ1Wdj4nx_E55KchGhcOY2f_z2DPQ==) [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGqWowAM_JVqdnChFWM1se3_p4mTWGzHNQpW9yB24RQv_VQNtKUpk29HR740yMA980dABbftXbUFkh-os2jd-BFc712EJ2d2D4wLYr595N8q0YET2TC1BVQjJsOXRZaWRgEpJfwIrINQODovoops1bTYhAoxQ==) This curvature dictates the paths that objects, including light, follow. Planets orbit the Sun not due to a direct pull, but because they are following the curves in spacetime created by the Sun's mass. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEWDZKYrR3gNukj5QQ90447emikv_0L2sqwMzy7_9JLxi58q9FPc0heoVqIF9wLQ4_Hh0GlD8H2GhbimKkGMTypjuS3viZscpjRSwH9l6O4VXs_z5zpcf0oaA30oz-HVCnnQzvK6g==)
*   **Principle of Equivalence:** Einstein suggested that the effects of gravity are indistinguishable from the effects of acceleration. [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQH7hr6RuGSJZvfVal5Amp82MIfIIHpKWgxvV7TFnQVu6SD2hOzvan50-QLabfartUyQjrXxJdzHMCt4LrftQfa-lcVRqNcEy3viq5Kh3oXO2ZZ1Wdj4nx_E55KchGhcOY2f_z2DPQ==)
*   **Gravitational Time Dilation:** Time also passes more slowly in stronger gravitational fields. This effect, along with time dilation caused by motion, is crucial for the accuracy of technologies like GPS satellites. [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG0tQE9KkECnGYoSOhcMJjESFs-gjo0FXdUiFffXstmip7z0hJ4tFNfq_HMKiRywwBoFMsVb32Vf5WYAcTFRQRpvCgoQfa81uV6GWnv2APiVYhhfSqc0vammP8cgROVvMds-u2uHGWfO3Xrcv_4xQ7U9bcjXQ==) [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFEUZguswNrhT12_P3N82FYtHxlIJ9-v3nyB45hooC1-omZi-qFPwkuiJuyOkh8upWl8ffOF5tczOuHY57ihzTgjW1R3S1v_V0aTJm8wyTkixAqD5jvzR4gb1zeNUNTxwGUjuzHIw==)

General relativity has accurately predicted phenomena such as black holes and gravitational waves, which have since been observed, further validating Einstein's theories. [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG-qrlt57UKl735Vi_bNuaozaKGgb9pRK06eIrPRF10hRfSt4cGZL8OA3IsDqXu5fVngFa3pDYGc8FZGzgmgsrGk3uASQbtbJ5uPbTuJnZdafTSvJoRydCa_8TqdFZS-i1VGIgJg-U5TZjOFeM=) [youtube](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFEUZguswNrhT12_P3N82FYtHxlIJ9-v3nyB45hooC1-omZi-qFPwkuiJuyOkh8upWl8ffOF5tczOuHY57ihzTgjW1R3S1v_V0aTJm8wyTkixAqD5jvzR4gb1zeNUNTxwGUjuzHIw==) The theory of relativity has fundamentally transformed physics and astronomy, superseding Newtonian mechanics and providing the framework for understanding the universe at all scales. [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQG-qrlt57UKl735Vi_bNuaozaKGgb9pRK06eIrPRF10hRfSt4cGZL8OA3IsDqXu5fVngFa3pDYGc8FZGzgmgsrGk3uASQbtbJ5uPbTuJnZdafTSvJoRydCa_8TqdFZS-i1VGIgJg-U5TZjOFeM=)

@eval(project="gemini-deep-research-agent", version="v1", name="research_agent")
def run_agent(
    question: str,
    initial_queries: int = 3,
    max_loops: int = 2,
    reasoning_model: str = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
) -> str:
    """
    Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
    """
    state = {
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content=question)],
        "initial_search_query_count": initial_queries,
        "max_research_loops": max_loops,
        "reasoning_model": reasoning_model,
    }
    result = graph.invoke(state)
    messages = result.get("messages", [])
    return messages[-1].content if messages else ""

code.doc: Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
code.signature: (question: str, initial_queries: int = 3, max_loops: int = 2, reasoning_model: str = 'gemini-2.5-flash-lite') -> str
code.source:
@eval(project="gemini-deep-research-agent", version="v1", name="research_agent")
def run_agent(
    question: str,
    initial_queries: int = 3,
    max_loops: int = 2,
    reasoning_model: str = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
) -> str:
    """
    Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
    """
    state = {
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content=question)],
        "initial_search_query_count": initial_queries,
        "max_research_loops": max_loops,
        "reasoning_model": reasoning_model,
    }
    result = graph.invoke(state)
    messages = result.get("messages", [])
    return messages[-1].content if messages else ""

code.doc: Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
code.signature: (question: str, initial_queries: int = 3, max_loops: int = 2, reasoning_model: str = 'gemini-2.5-flash-lite') -> str
code.source:
@eval(project="gemini-deep-research-agent", version="v1", name="research_agent")
def run_agent(
    question: str,
    initial_queries: int = 3,
    max_loops: int = 2,
    reasoning_model: str = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
) -> str:
    """
    Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
    """
    state = {
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content=question)],
        "initial_search_query_count": initial_queries,
        "max_research_loops": max_loops,
        "reasoning_model": reasoning_model,
    }
    result = graph.invoke(state)
    messages = result.get("messages", [])
    return messages[-1].content if messages else ""

kwargs.question: What are black holes and how are they formed?

output:
Black holes are cosmic objects formed through various processes, broadly categorized into stellar, supermassive, and primordial black holes. Recent research is significantly refining our understanding of their formation, particularly concerning their origins in the early universe and through merger events.

**Stellar Black Hole Formation:**
The most common way stellar black holes are thought to form is through the gravitational collapse of massive stars at the end of their life cycle. However, recent findings from gravitational wave detectors like LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA are challenging some basic predictions of stellar evolution theory. By 2024, over 100 binary black hole merger events had been detected [kyoto-u](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=2). Some of these detected mergers, such as GW241011 and GW241110 in late 2024, exhibit unusual spin characteristics. These anomalies suggest that some black holes are "second-generation" black holes, meaning they formed from previous black hole mergers in dense environments like star clusters. The observation of a black hole spinning in the opposite direction of its orbit, as seen in GW241110, strongly supports this theory of hierarchical mergers [innovationnewsnetwork](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=3) [eurekalert](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=4) [techno-science](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEF0cmBESkrc4LmWACLZRfwWb1zTYFm3gRZ57dDK1tBhRf0VupQsNVN-NGwuAhQCkEs8bpUwEMW_GHiytglWu7RGstLQKbffZXTIlQlEf7iVoUegh34SwHD-1A7EUHCjcmb7n_Sfe_nYKr0jmT123-gqvOXFHREdnuz3Y3kX6fKNaECQFpFUFgrbr4UkCtHUw-7TMugvCf879Vg). These merger events also offer precise tests of Einstein's general theory of relativity and provide insights into the astrophysical mechanisms of black hole formation [innovationnewsnetwork](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=3) [eurekalert](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=4).

**Supermassive Black Hole Formation:**
Supermassive black holes (SMBHs), millions to billions of times the mass of our Sun, present a significant puzzle, especially their presence very early in the universe. The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has detected SMBHs that existed much earlier than previously thought, prompting a re-evaluation of formation models [interstellar](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEmpqTM3_aSiHX87gA9gMZpWnbTvOu3y1FvLwGvGQiA1qC1DFs_cMRquIcCfXjk9JrYJG6gxN6OBoghw93sBo7j7sxEFMqpZQHuY3xhIp-4yFO_SLFHs7n2P6fGwmKPBqd8ZUMq3M0QzbzN0ObjNTD0YG9u6Uo0Vw00btdaEWJjBMFO4MS-OVsJTckF6ELxDMU9U_51unF3wyF9soOmFFiSwAffhlgflCxf1Ts=) [livescience](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=). One SMBH, LID-568, formed about 1.5 billion years after the Big Bang and is accreting material at an extraordinary rate [interstellar](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEmpqTM3_aSiHX87gA9gMZpWnbTvOu3y1FvLwGvGQiA1qC1DFs_cMRquIcCfXjk9JrYJG6gxN6OBoghw93sBo7j7sxEFMqpZQHuY3xhIp-4yFO_SLFHs7n2P6fGwmKPBqd8ZUMq3M0QzbzN0ObjNTD0YG9u6Uo0Vw00btdaEWJjBMFO4MS-OVsJTckF6ELxDMU9U_51unF3wyF9soOmFFiSwAffhlgflCxf1Ts=) [livescience](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=). Two primary theories for the origin of these early SMBHs are:
*   **Formation from the First Stars:** Some theories propose that SMBHs originated from the very first stars, known as Population III.1 stars. These stars grew to immense sizes and, upon their death, could have seeded the formation of SMBHs [sci](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGS1RLJ1-WJ4-SfSZqQa84euRPe39q_GMcz3xy8nLdZKb3W9NKMnXSQ1l-OYMu5TcbkAHqB-CdKD_3EBQONtqKuWO9f4swUmnR88sXEEiebu0gM1BkM-0hrHpLsx2gVQ1zAztHvN1_OADvMZlbHmnBpakdm7o1l6qHDtJcRXo2sEciSC4ZnqMGuSnCfzef3GTwKWf7lRTq9N2H-ppV0_XUGmg==).
*   **Direct Collapse:** Another leading theory, the direct collapse black hole (DCBH) model, suggests that massive black hole seeds formed directly from the gravitational collapse of large, metal-free gas clouds in the early universe, bypassing stellar evolution entirely [nasa](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGTQha0XiLm55efqz5Otxbk8FzoGdJgbqPxd0SqVb1Kd74dpPPrK2S_UQQ6KQThA83lBGwrzdhhLLCqAjSl3zTC4yYW2cphPeDHSjfNArNGCkJe1IQdb7kt1yYSnuIoUIduCpPA7Ga8jAzr0L3Uyvu1jmvntI3UWhsNj8HlPy0EVTzfzMTf5480Cs9RtgCyxOD41CCIUPn15k8y00b0lfs=) [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEHIt1kW9XmfpgkNfzRjcn4-bBM9i43FwE-li8TaMJ7W4p_rP-5fXwQvlPVAfAgXy50lC-0HIXjfNooAW1tCZGDVZ27MLz3ZP5Ezxv8ZKxkI9IWTtoUZuxXS6Xy8v_Q8IFpLUNohaxE0s_sIaGKmgzZ0jAN). This process requires specific conditions, including a metal-free environment, atomic cooling, and a sufficient flux of Lyman-Werner photons to prevent fragmentation of the gas cloud [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEHIt1kW9XmfpgkNfzRjcn4-bBM9i43FwE-li8TaMJ7W4p_rP-5fXwQvlPVAfAgXy50lC-0HIXjfNooAW1tCZGDVZ27MLz3ZP5Ezxv8ZKxkI9IWTtoUZuxXS6Xy8v_Q8IFpLUNohaxE0s_sIaGKmgzZ0jAN). Evidence for this scenario is being investigated in galaxies like the Infinity Galaxy [nasa](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGTQha0XiLm55efqz5Otxbk8FzoGdJgbqPxd0SqVb1Kd74dpPPrK2S_UQQ6KQThA83lBGwrzdhhLLCqAjSl3zTC4yYW2cphPeDHSjfNArNGCkJe1IQdb7kt1yYSnuIoUIduCpPA7Ga8jAzr0L3Uyvu1jmvntI3UWhsNj8HlPy0EVTzfzMTf5480Cs9RtgCyxOD41CCIUPn15k8y00b0lfs=).
The rapid growth of SMBHs in the early universe, even in smaller galaxies, is another area of intense study. Observations of the galaxy CANUCS-LRD-z8.6, existing less than 600 million years after the Big Bang, show a central black hole that is more massive than its host galaxy, defying typical mass-galaxy relationships and suggesting accelerated growth [esawebb](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQF1ZAhN7LLtEqUYo_cnEtUWSb-FshHMZVd7fv-NI4OviIEAt4xQPMql8fqYNHVMVD6t2u14j62VE2T7KVxRiEvToCGQMODId2lZjmK3GXefJFidajoMpSeKw23WZ0Y=) [space](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHOWfe5XkYDpJDLv_uU6kzc9ycnSJuER4CYb1xR0zhalNevVWRihKzCX69EFt2iAOVE590u2A-SrdOTiPiIbzrwIZKPDRq7abUaWKwbT8vqDg0da0gIvAq5UPzSiSCrV_hHGgtixe5hr1s9Tx5S2Stb4DBMM4avq0RoFI-KccbojIGyxN6uzJilXLfxIUbKa7QiPy8=).

**Primordial Black Hole Theories:**
Primordial black holes (PBHs) are hypothetical objects believed to have formed in the first fraction of a second after the Big Bang from the collapse of extremely dense regions [theguardian](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGEayiw7f5_FGRZbqoUI2uB7cIo46PZIQxFHaro_fX2P85vUzUX7oHn2Ab89kArcNLHNbfimYQwY6dy46l9tlU8WLiCeeEnoRUS_CArVwSrDvsuRaSI6ysGPVKq0ezIYs2Ow08PNFsSkbMUkfswi8cMvmyUbPVCgOVaLnTg-9FPZtMqvGprAMin4Z-VJHK1y2VSBvjWu1bMVZZOgTEDnHBGU4JlPg==) [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHms_P5n63DEdXAxXjaHVKEla-xzgTJY8xcIENFN0GIYUCXd2iZ6rgO79pLewN9agmUcrYb1FFPf83nfgiy03vARbnXXUcGbnYSKTAcpO9zNyP60w0xgavUT8UHAIVJguKzlMzZ6v23WcVKps88Qg==). These early cosmic seeds could have influenced the formation of early galaxies [theguardian](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGEayiw7f5_FGRZbqoUI2uB7cIo46PZIQxFHaro_fX2P85vUzUX7oHn2Ab89kArcNLHNbfimYQwY6dy46l9tlU8WLiCeeEnoRUS_CArVwSrDvsuRaSI6ysGPVKq0ezIYs2Ow08PNFsSkbMUkfswi8cMvmyUbPVCgOVaLnTg-9FPZtMqvGprAMin4Z-VJHK1y2VSBvjWu1bMVZZOgTEDnHBGU4JlPg==). Recent interest in PBHs has been reignited by JWST observations, including a "nearly naked" black hole with minimal surrounding material, which could be evidence for a PBH and challenges the conventional view of black hole formation after stars [theguardian](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQGEayiw7f5_FGRZbqoUI2uB7cIo46PZIQxFHaro_fX2P85vUzUX7oHn2Ab89kArcNLHNbfimYQwY6dy46l9tlU8WLiCeeEnoRUS_CArVwSrDvsuRaSI6ysGPVKq0ezIYs2Ow08PNFsSkbMUkfswi8cMvmyUbPVCgOVaLnTg-9FPZtMqvGprAMin4Z-VJHK1y2VSBvjWu1bMVZZOgTEDnHBGU4JlPg==). PBHs are also considered potential explanations for the unexpectedly large early galaxies observed by JWST and for gravitational wave events involving smaller-than-solar-mass black holes detected in late 2025 [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHms_P5n63DEdXAxXjaHVKEla-xzgTJY8xcIENFN0GIYUCXd2iZ6rgO79pLewN9agmUcrYb1FFPf83nfgiy03vARbnXXUcGbnYSKTAcpO9zNyP60w0xgavUT8UHAIVJguKzlMzZ6v23WcVKps88Qg==). Mechanisms for PBH formation include density fluctuations during inflation, cosmological phase transitions, and cosmic strings [mdpi](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQEwbQtl3RLmrVtxwWi9BZYOhO6y-_RiYm8HOK4HQJJ_f-C75SYR-9O3ChQRAiO-KvgygaRMch5tBT0MxRwMksP__h69Qgtb_gKrJWW9NgPc6_H9NQ7NzuYCOi2l3dnjW80=) [wikipedia](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQFO9feCIPQ73Ej1xgrS_ntQRUTDHnBM157czYqhKIpJTKxq_E83yvXn8zFhMVsv0dZ57iFzA-4w_SYeRGD-M73uykEcsk7a6XPN4M5nDhAeWuvD0brfn9shgmr3M8ta8uxUsUMlCS-X61wDEIaQyw==). Researchers are also exploring the possibility that PBHs constitute dark matter [mpg](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHo_m1qcunED8U8Bn-dmocHliBx2reSaCWygCqeOvscSUEVea7CzPN3L3I9d6wg10SBbb05HjaBSl4D9kQKrTH5W_8C86O7SOmQ9_iua12Pr-8m-1RDlfL_2m5yVNn4tlxLleiOPr48HT3qulUGRGYM8jrE6JNitZPJRUMlL2zE3sp_osD4hJo5nwW-ZGtTl3Gh2FNcRPE=1).

In summary, black hole formation is understood through the collapse of massive stars, the direct collapse of gas clouds in the early universe, and potentially from the initial conditions of the Big Bang itself. Ongoing research, particularly from the JWST and gravitational wave observatories, continues to refine these theories, revealing the complex and diverse ways these enigmatic objects come into existence.

code.doc: Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
code.signature: (question: str, initial_queries: int = 3, max_loops: int = 2, reasoning_model: str = 'gemini-2.5-flash-lite') -> str
code.source:
@eval(project="gemini-deep-research-agent", version="v1", name="research_agent")
def run_agent(
    question: str,
    initial_queries: int = 3,
    max_loops: int = 2,
    reasoning_model: str = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
) -> str:
    """
    Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
    """
    state = {
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content=question)],
        "initial_search_query_count": initial_queries,
        "max_research_loops": max_loops,
        "reasoning_model": reasoning_model,
    }
    result = graph.invoke(state)
    messages = result.get("messages", [])
    return messages[-1].content if messages else ""

This process involves your immune system creating specific antibodies designed to combat that particular pathogen [hopkinsmedicine](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHQvdYmBE2uAkQM13FuaNocf3Pv6B2_6ESQzITNaHnLFkMB_xj4suKPlrq-yfN_XZgYgCQVWFMymLIgUJv6L7cyqyUlICgexuCWatrOBSaZmN-1vlCx9bK3NGV0PeWa89FYg0G_pl3nPnGWMu6HDNSgYKcSvH_Y1pWdgFaCpK-p1ikg4uslWtBJ). Vaccines can be formulated with killed or altered germs, harmless components of germs, or instructions for your body to produce harmless germ parts [hopkinsmedicine](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHQvdYmBE2uAkQM13FuaNocf3Pv6B2_6ESQzITNaHnLFkMB_xj4suKPlrq-yfN_XZgYgCQVWFMymLIgUJv6L7cyqyUlICgexuCWatrOBSaZmN-1vlCx9bK3NGV0PeWa89FYg0G_pl3nPnGWMu6HDNSgYKcSvH_Y1pWdgFaCpK-p1ikg4uslWtBJ).

When your body encounters the antigen from a vaccine, specialized immune cells like B-cells and T-cells are activated [hopkinsmedicine](https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/grounding-api-redirect/AUZIYQHQvdYmBE2uAkQM13FuaNocf3Pv6B2_6ESQzITNaHnLFkMB_xj4suKPlrq-yfN_XZgYgCQVWFMymLIgUJv6L7cyqyUlICgexuCWatrOBSaZmN-1vlCx9bK3NGV0PeWa89FYg0G_pl3nPnGWMu6HDNSgYKcSvH_Y1pWdgFaCpK-p1ikg4uslWtBJ). code.doc: Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
code.signature: (question: str, initial_queries: int = 3, max_loops: int = 2, reasoning_model: str = 'gemini-2.5-flash-lite') -> str
code.source:
@eval(project="gemini-deep-research-agent", version="v1", name="research_agent")
def run_agent(
    question: str,
    initial_queries: int = 3,
    max_loops: int = 2,
    reasoning_model: str = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
) -> str:
    """
    Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
    """
    state = {
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content=question)],
        "initial_search_query_count": initial_queries,
        "max_research_loops": max_loops,
        "reasoning_model": reasoning_model,
    }
    result = graph.invoke(state)
    messages = result.get("messages", [])
    return messages[-1].content if messages else ""

code.doc: Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
code.signature: (question: str, initial_queries: int = 3, max_loops: int = 2, reasoning_model: str = 'gemini-2.5-flash-lite') -> str
code.source:
@eval(project="gemini-deep-research-agent", version="v1", name="research_agent")
def run_agent(
    question: str,
    initial_queries: int = 3,
    max_loops: int = 2,
    reasoning_model: str = "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
) -> str:
    """
    Main LLM-facing entrypoint for the research agent. Wrapped with @eval so calls are traced/stored.
    """
    state = {
        "messages": [HumanMessage(content=question)],
        "initial_search_query_count": initial_queries,
        "max_research_loops": max_loops,
        "reasoning_model": reasoning_model,
    }
    result = graph.invoke(state)
    messages = result.get("messages", [])
    return messages[-1].content if messages else ""
